fr_pecher_verb.hook: A tug on the line – Monsieur Verbe FISHES; think of a PEACHY little fish (pay-SHAY).
fr_pecher_verb.why: Pêcher = to fish (la pêche = fishing; careful, also la pêche = peach). Regular -er: RED beret.
ex: Il pêche dans la rivière.
He fishes in the river.

fr_drainer_verb.hook: A little ditch and – whoosh – the puddle DRAINS away (dray-NAY).
fr_drainer_verb.why: Drain → drainer = to drain. Regular -er: RED beret.
ex: Il draine la flaque avec sa pelle.
He drains the puddle with his spade.

fr_rejaillir_verb.hook: Plop goes the pebble – and the water JUMPS back up on him: rejaillir (ruh-zhah-YEER).
fr_rejaillir_verb.why: Jaillir = to gush → rejaillir = to splash back; figuratively to reflect on someone. Regular -ir (nous …issons): GREEN beret.
ex: L'eau rejaillit sur son pantalon.
The water splashes back onto his pants.

fr_survoler_verb.hook: High above the water, the bird kite flies OVER – it SUR-VOLE the river (sewr-voh-LAY).
fr_survoler_verb.why: Sur = over + voler = to fly → survoler = to fly over; also to skim (a text). Regular -er: RED beret.
ex: Son cerf-volant survole la rivière.
His kite flies over the river.

fr_deverser_verb.hook: Hand mirror up: the stream POURS itself into the pool – se déverser (day-vehr-SAY).
fr_deverser_verb.why: Verser = to pour → se déverser = to flow, to pour out (into). The hand mirror shows it is reflexive (se). Regular -er: RED beret.
ex: Le ruisseau se déverse dans la mare.
The stream pours into the pond.

fr_pomper_verb.hook: Up, down, up, down – Monsieur Verbe PUMPS water from the well (pohn-PAY).
fr_pomper_verb.why: Pump → pomper = to pump. Regular -er: RED beret.

fr_etinceler_verb.hook: Twinkle! The diamond gives off little sparks – une ÉTINCELLE, a spark: it SPARKLES (ay-tan-suh-LAY).
fr_etinceler_verb.why: Une étincelle = a spark → étinceler = to sparkle, to glitter. Regular -er (il étincelle): RED beret.
ex: Le diamant étincelle au soleil.
The diamond sparkles in the sun.

fr_polluer_verb.hook: A plastic bottle in the gray puddle – litter POLLUTES the water (poh-LWAY).
fr_polluer_verb.why: Pollute → polluer = to pollute. Regular -er: RED beret.
ex: Les déchets polluent la rivière.
Litter pollutes the river.

fr_rayonner_verb.hook: Golden RAYS all around – Monsieur Verbe RADIATES joy (reh-yoh-NAY).
fr_rayonner_verb.why: Un rayon = a ray → rayonner = to radiate, to beam. Regular -er: RED beret.
ex: Il rayonne de bonheur.
He is beaming with happiness.

fr_jucher_verb.hook: Up on the tall stool, hand mirror in hand – Monsieur Verbe PERCHES himself: se jucher (zhew-SHAY).
fr_jucher_verb.why: Se jucher = to perch (oneself) up high. The hand mirror shows it is reflexive (se). Regular -er: RED beret.
ex: Il se juche sur un grand tabouret.
He perches himself on a tall stool.

fr_germer_verb.hook: Pop, pop! Tiny green shoots – the seeds GERMINATE (zhehr-MAY).
fr_germer_verb.why: Germinate → germer = to sprout, to germinate. Regular -er: RED beret.
ex: Les graines commencent à germer.
The seeds are starting to sprout.

fr_enfanter_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe the museum guide points politely to the plaque: enfanter = to give birth (literary), from un ENFANT, a child (ahn-fahn-TAY).
fr_enfanter_verb.why: Shown only as a museum plaque, nothing drawn. Literary/old-fashioned; everyday French says accoucher or donner naissance. Regular -er: RED beret.
ex: Dans les vieux contes, la reine enfante une princesse.
In old tales, the queen gives birth to a princess.

fr_bronzer_verb.hook: Sunglasses on, deckchair out – Monsieur Verbe turns BRONZE: he TANS (brohn-ZAY).
fr_bronzer_verb.why: Bronze → bronzer = to tan, to sunbathe. Regular -er: RED beret.
ex: Il bronze dans sa chaise longue.
He is sunbathing in his deckchair.

fr_carburer_verb.hook: Glug! Like a CARBURETOR on fuel, Monsieur Verbe RUNS on coffee: carburer (kahr-bew-RAY).
fr_carburer_verb.why: Carburer (informal) = to run on, to be fueled by; to work hard. Regular -er: RED beret.
ex: Ce matin, il carbure au café.
This morning he runs on coffee.
